title: Noodle-Shaped Thai Beef Satay
description: A paleo-friendly, nostalgic Thai dish from the streets of Bangkok featuring beef brisket in a winey, light sauce. Serve with a side of fresh cucumber slices.
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine coconut aminos, fish sauce, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, lemongrass, coriander, and red pepper flakes. Blend until smooth.
Heat 2 tablespoons of coconut oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Pour the blended sauce mixture into the saucepan and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the sauce is cooking, slice the beef brisket into thin strips and set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix together nigiri rice flour and vegetable oil until a dough forms.
Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces and shape each piece into a long, thin noodle.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of coconut oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef strips and cook for 3-4 minutes, or until browned and cooked through.
Add the cooked beef strips to the noodle dough, one at a time, and wrap the dough around each strip to form a satay shape.
Cook the satays in the skillet for an additional 2-3 minutes, or until the dough is cooked through and lightly browned.
Serve the satays hot with the winey sauce from the saucepan and a side of fresh cucumber slices.
